findings.comment: If `start > chain.received_log.count()`, then `end` will be clamped to `chain.received_log.count()`, resulting in `start > end`. Passing an inverted range `start..end` to `read` can panic or cause runtime errors in Rust range slicing depending on the underlying collection/view implementation.

Breaking only when `received_entries < CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES` is fragile if the remote validator runs a different limit (e.g. an older validator that returns all entries, or a future validator version with a smaller limit, or if `received_entries == 0`). Specifically, if `received_entries == 0` when `CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES == 0` (or if remote returns empty when offset is beyond total, though handled here if `0 < CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES`), an infinite loop can occur if the validator returned a batch equal to a smaller limit or if offset does not advance. Furthermore, if a validator has a limit smaller than `CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES`, it will terminate prematurely before fetching all entries.
